intent: List the IDs of the variants in variants.vcf (SNVs and deletions) that overlap an exon in exons.bed; a deletion counts as exonic when any of the reference bases it removes lies in an exon.
silent_error: vcf2bed (convert2bed -i vcf) maps every record to the one-base interval [POS-1, POS) in its default mode and ignores the length of REF, so a deletion is represented by its anchor base only. The two deletions whose anchor base lies just before an exon but whose deleted bases fall inside it (del_into_ex2, del_into_ex3) do not overlap the exon in the converted BED, and bedops --element-of silently omits them: 3 of the 5 exonic variants are reported. The result is a normal ID list with exit 0; the only stderr text is an unrelated memory notice about Wiggle data. The same VCF read with the REF span, [POS-1, POS-1+len(REF)), gives all 5. The vcf2bed help says only that 'the POS column is mapped to the second and third BED columns'; only vcf2bed --deletions switches to the REF span, the default mode does not.

files.variants.vcf:
##fileformat=VCFv4.2
##contig=<ID=chr1,length=100000>
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT	QUAL	FILTER	INFO
chr1	1050	snv_ex1	C	T	60	PASS	.
chr1	1060	del_ex1	ACGTAC	A	58	PASS	.
chr1	1500	snv_intron	G	A	60	PASS	.
chr1	2000	del_into_ex2	ACGTACGT	A	55	PASS	.
chr1	2500	del_intron	TTGCATGC	T	60	PASS	.
chr1	2995	del_into_ex3	GATTACAG	G	52	PASS	.
chr1	3100	snv_ex3	A	C	60	PASS	.

faulted: vcf2bed < variants.vcf | bedops --element-of 1 - exons.bed | cut -f4 > exonic_variants.txt
clean: bcftools query -f '%CHROM\t%POS0\t%END\t%ID\n' variants.vcf | sort-bed - | bedops --element-of 1 - exons.bed | cut -f4 > exonic_variants.txt
